$comment: Copy to .quality-kernel/tools.json in your project and adjust. Two consumers: (1) the REFEREE reads the top-level verify/productionGlobs/acceptance/linkPaths; (2) the forge cleaner/hardener read the per-language tools below. COMMIT this file — the referee reads it from the base ref (it is never trusted from the worktree).
$refereeContract: The referee verifies a committed base..head. It rebuilds the FULL BASE TREE and overlays ONLY the files matching productionGlobs from head, then runs verify (and acceptance if set) against that tree — so tests/fixtures/helpers/runners cannot be tampered by the change to force a green. Every changed path must be production (overlaid+verified), a declared test (executed), or a manifest (field-checked); anything else => indeterminate. Declare docs/prompts/config/assets in productionGlobs so anything read at runtime is verified (overlaying prose is harmless).
$testGlobsHelp: The immutable suite THIS repo declares — stays at base (never overlaid) and is executed. Kept separate from route's broad tier heuristic so a production file merely NAMED like a test (lib/spec/**, *-test.*) is not silently treated as harness.
$acceptanceHelp: Optional. A human-approved, machine-checkable criteria command DISTINCT from the coder's own tests (Constitution P3). Lives outside productionGlobs so it stays immutable-from-base. Example: "node --test acceptance/*.mjs".
$linkPathsHelp: Opt-in (default []). Dependency dirs symlinked from the worktree into the trusted tree. This is a TRUST HOLE: a build in the verify chain could write THROUGH the symlink into your real worktree, and a tampered dep is not audited. Prefer verifySetup (e.g. 'npm ci --ignore-scripts') to provision deps hermetically from the base lockfile.
$outputGlobsHelp: Paths the verify/build chain is ALLOWED to create in the tree (e.g. ['dist/**','coverage/**']). Everything the chain writes outside these (and outside node_modules/.venv/vendor/.git) makes the run indeterminate — so a build cannot plant a module the immutable tests then import.
